title: [Audit] System index requests (raw)
description: The newest 1,000 requests against .kibana*, .security*, .alerts-* and other dot-prefixed indices, one row per index named — privileged data access that deserves a second look. Backing indices of ordinary data streams (.ds-logs-…) and shard-level copies of a request are left out. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.
esql: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | KEEP @timestamp, actor, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, client.ip | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 1000 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor) | RENAME @timestamp AS Time, actor AS Identity, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices AS Index, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action AS `Transport action`, client.ip AS `Client IP`
